successCriteria.description: Define the `LeavePolicy` interface in `src/modules/leave/leave-policy.model.ts` with all specified fields: id, policyName, leaveType (imported from `src/shared/types/index.ts`), entitlementDays, accrualRate, maxAccumulation, minimumNoticeDays, requiresManagerApproval, isActive, allowsNegativeBalance, maxConsecutiveDays, createdAt, updatedAt.

Define `ILeavePolicyRepository` interface in `src/modules/leave/leave-policy.repository.ts` with methods: `findById(id: string): Promise<LeavePolicy | null>`, `findAll(): Promise<LeavePolicy[]>`, `findByLeaveType(leaveType: LeaveType): Promise<LeavePolicy[]>`, `create(data): Promise<LeavePolicy>`, `update(id: string, data): Promise<LeavePolicy>`, `softDelete(id: string): Promise<void>`.
Implement `LeavePolicyRepository` class extending `BaseRepository<LeavePolicy>` and implementing `ILeavePolicyRepository`, with all six methods delegating to `this.query()` for database access.
Include Jest unit tests at `tests/unit/modules/leave/leave-policy.repository.test.ts` covering all repository methods with mocked pool.

constraints: GP-001: All database access must go through the repository pattern — `LeavePolicyRepository` extends `BaseRepository<LeavePolicy>` and uses `this.query()` for all DB calls.
no-any (HARNESS.json): Use `unknown` with type guards instead of `any` — repository method signatures and query params must avoid `any`.
no-direct-db-outside-repository (HARNESS.json): No inline SQL outside the repository layer — the repository is the sole DB access point for leave policies.
GP-006: No unhandled promise rejections — all async repository methods must propagate errors cleanly; tests must handle rejected promises.
Strict TypeScript (no implicit any, strict null checks) — all interface fields and method signatures must be fully typed.
outOfScope: Database migrations / table creation for `leave_policy` — this phase only defines the model interface and repository; actual schema is deferred.
LeavePolicy service layer, controller, and routes — these are Phase 6–8 per PLAN.md.
LeaveBalance and LeaveRequest models/repositories — these are Phase 4 and Phase 5 respectively.
Audit logging (GP-002) — the repository alone does not trigger state-changing operations; audit integration happens at the service layer in Phase 6.
RBAC enforcement (GP-005) — enforced at middleware/route layer, not at the repository level.
